title: Microsoft Purview: Purview SDK built into Microsoft Agent Framework for custom agents
summary: The default-state field needs correction: Microsoft identifies developer implementation as the opt-in mechanism, rather than leaving who enables the integration unspecified. The documented policy controls, licensing prerequisites and paused-rollout notice are supported; the billing checklist also names a configuration missing from the controls table.

claims.claim: Both Python middleware types buffer a streamed response fully and prevent incremental output.
claims.quote: Both middleware types buffer a streamed response in full and evaluate it before releasing any update. Streaming therefore doesn't deliver content incrementally while Purview middleware is attached.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Purview portal does not currently support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered applications.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Entra-registered DLP portal PowerShell. Opened use-the-api: "The Microsoft Purview portal doesn't currently support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered applications." Also read ai-entra-registered.

claims.claim: The printed New-DlpComplianceRule call can block UploadText matching the credit card number sensitive information type in the named policy.
claims.quote: -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name = "credit card number"}  -GenerateAlert $true -GenerateIncidentReport @("siteadmin") -NotifyUser @("admin@contonso.onmicrosoft.com") -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="UploadText";value="Block"})

claims.claim: Example 4 in the linked rule reference creates the policy before creating its rule.
claims.quote: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name "Test Entra DLP" -Mode Enable -Locations $locations -EnforcementPlanes @("Application")

claims.claim: This DLP policy is scoped to a specific Entra-registered AI app and blocks prompts based on sensitive information types.
claims.quote: Support today is only available for a DLP policy that blocks prompts based on sensitive information types. This requires the configuration of a PowerShell cmdlet that's scoped to a specific Entra-registered AI app.

claims.claim: DSPM for AI reports provide the Enterprise AI apps category for these interactions.

claims.claim: The Purview portal's Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention Policies route reaches retention-policy creation.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, navigate to Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention Policies and create a retention policy
claims.fix: Replace the retention sentence with: "The interactions can also be retained: Learn says to go to Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention Policies in the Microsoft Purview portal and create a retention policy for the Enterprise AI apps location." This retains the correct route and makes the omitted policy-creation step explicit.

claims.claim: Enterprise AI apps is the retention location for Entra-registered AI-app interactions.
claims.quote: create a retention policy to retain interactions with Entra-registered AI apps by selecting the location Enterprise AI apps and specify the required retention period.

claims.claim: DLP and collection policies are configured in the tenant, separately from attaching middleware in agent code.
claims.quote: Have your tenant admin configure Microsoft Purview policies and settings.

claims.claim: The cited pages describe no tenant-level inventory or requirement that shows or mandates which custom agents attach this middleware.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Agent Framework tenant middleware inventory enforcement; Purview Agent Framework tenant enable require middleware admin setting. Read the integration and developer pages; no inventory or mandate of middleware attachment found.

claims.claim: The Agent Framework integration page shows a client ID but does not describe the required Microsoft Graph permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Agent Framework permissions consent Content.Process.User. Read the full integration page: client_id="<clientId>" but no Graph permissions. The use-the-api tutorial gives permissions for experimentation, not production-deployment planning.

claims.claim: An app must enforce a returned blocking policy action.
claims.quote: In this example, `restrictAccess` means that your app must block the user from the requested action.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Every configuration the governance checklist tells readers to check has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Confirm pay-as-you-go billing is set up and budgeted against an Azure subscription before the middleware is deployed." The controls table has only DLP and collection-policy rows.
claims.fix: Replace that Before rollout bullet with: "Review expected pay-as-you-go consumption with FinOps before the middleware is deployed." This preserves budgeting advice without directing readers to check an unlisted configuration control.
